content: 1. Matteelli A, Shubber Z, Hermans S, Meintjes G, Grinsztejn B, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2016 to investigate tuberculosis (TB) as a cause of hospitalization and in-hospital mortality among people living with HIV worldwide. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society. 2. Gaskell KM, Feasey NA, and Heyderman RS reviewed the management of severe non-TB bacterial infections in HIV-infected adults in 2015. Their work was published in the Expert Review of Anti-Infective Therapy. 3. Ford N, Shubber Z, Meintjes G, Grinsztejn B, Eholie S, Mills EJ, et al. performed a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2015 to identify the causes of hospital admissions among people living with HIV globally. Their findings were published in The Lancet HIV. 4. Rajasingham R, Smith RM, Park BJ, Jarvis JN, Govender NP, Chiller TM, et al. updated the global burden of disease analysis for HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis in 2017. Their study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 5. Bahr NC, Antinori S, Wheat LJ, and Sarosi GA reviewed histoplasmosis infections worldwide in 2015, emphasizing the need to consider this disease outside the Ohio River Valley. Their findings were published in Current Tropical Medicine Reports. 6. Caceres DH and Valdes A explored the co-occurrence of histoplasmosis and tuberculosis in people with advanced HIV in 2019. Their study was published in the Journal of Fungi (Basel). 7. Wang Z-D, Wang S-C, Liu H-H, Ma H-Y, Li Z-Y, Wei F, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2017 to determine the prevalence and burden of Toxoplasma gondii infection in HIV-infected individuals. Their findings were published in The Lancet HIV. 8. Le T, Wolbers M, Chi NH, Quang VM, Chinh NT, Huong Lan NP, et al. studied the epidemiology, seasonality, and predictors of outcomes for AIDS-associated Penicillium marneffei infection in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, in 2011. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 9. Hu Y, Zhang J, Li X, Yang Y, Zhang Y, Ma J, et al. described Penicillium marneffei infection as an emerging disease in mainland China in 2013. Their study was published in Mycopathologia. 10. Schwartz IS, Govender NP, Sigler L, Jiang Y, Maphanga TG, Toplis B, et al. highlighted the global rise of new dimorphic fungal pathogens, including Emergomyces, in 2019. Their findings were published in PLoS Pathogens. 11. Ford N, Shubber Z, Saranchuk P, Pathai S, Durier N, O'Brien DP, et al. reviewed the burden of HIV-related cytomegalovirus retinitis in resource-limited settings in 2013. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 12. Vojnov L, Markby J, Boeke C, Harris L, Ford N, Peter T, et al. demonstrated that point-of-care CD4 testing improves linkage to HIV care and timeliness of antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation in a public health approach. Their systematic review and meta-analysis were published in PLoS One in 2016. 13. The World Health Organization (WHO) maintains a list of prequalified in vitro diagnostic products, which was accessed on June 1, 2021, for reference. 14. Mfinanga S, Chanda D, Kivuyo SL, Guinness L, Bottomley C, Simms V, et al. conducted an open-label, randomized controlled trial in 2015 to evaluate cryptococcal meningitis screening and community-based early adherence support in people with advanced HIV infection starting ART in Tanzania and Zambia. Their findings were published in The Lancet. 15. Hakim J, Musiime V, Szubert AJ, Mallewa J, Siika A, Agutu C, et al. investigated the impact of enhanced prophylaxis plus ART for advanced HIV infection in Africa in 2017. Their study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 16. The WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis prevention, screening, and diagnosis were accessed on June 1, 2021, for reference. 17. Bahr N, Boulware DR, Marais S, Scriven J, Wilkinson RJ, Meintjes G reviewed central nervous system immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome in 2013. Their findings were published in Current Infectious Disease Reports. 18. Lawn SD, Bekker L-G, Myer L, Orrell C, Wood R identified cryptococcal immune reconstitution disease as a major cause of early mortality in a South African ART program in 2005. Their study was published in AIDS. 19. Lawn SD, Harries AD, Anglaret X, Myer L, Wood R reviewed early mortality among adults accessing ART programs in sub-Saharan Africa in 2008. Their findings were published in AIDS. 20. Park BJ, Wannemuehler KA, Marston BJ, Govender N, Pappas PG, Chiller TM estimated the global burden of cryptococcal meningitis among people living with HIV/AIDS in 2009. Their study was published in AIDS. 21. Guidelines for the diagnosis, prevention, and management of cryptococcal disease in HIV-infected individuals were published as a supplement to the 2016 WHO consolidated guidelines on ART use. 22. The Southern African HIV Clinicians Society updated its guidelines for the prevention, diagnosis, and management of cryptococcal meningitis in HIV-infected individuals in 2013. 23. Ford N, Shubber Z, Jarvis JN, Chiller T, Greene G, Migone C, et al. reviewed CD4 cell count thresholds for cryptococcal antigen screening in HIV-infected individuals in 2018. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 24. Awotiwon AA, Rutherford GW, Meintjes G, Eshun-Wilson I reviewed primary antifungal prophylaxis for cryptococcal disease in HIV-positive individuals in 2018. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 25. Molloy SF, Kanyama C, Heyderman RS, Loyse A, Kouanfack C, Chanda D, et al. evaluated antifungal combinations for treating cryptococcal meningitis in Africa in 2018. Their study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 26. Tenforde MW, Shapiro AE, Rouse B, Jarvis JN, Li T, Eshun-Wilson I, et al. reviewed treatment options for HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis in 2018. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 27. Mootsikapun P, Chetchotisakd P, Anunnatsiri S, Choksawadphinyo K compared the efficacy of fluconazole and itraconazole as consolidation therapy for cryptococcal meningitis in AIDS patients in 2003. Their study was published in the Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand. 28. Van der Horst CM, Saag MS, Cloud GA, Hamill RJ, Graybill JR, Sobel JD, et al. evaluated treatment options for cryptococcal meningitis associated with AIDS in 1997. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 29. Bozzette SA, Larsen RA, Chiu J, Leal MAE, Jacobsen J, Rothman P, et al. conducted a placebo-controlled trial of maintenance therapy with fluconazole after treating cryptococcal meningitis in AIDS patients in 1991. Their study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 30. Saag MS, Cloud GA, Graybill JR, Sobel JD, Tuazon CU, Johnson PC, et al. compared itraconazole and fluconazole as maintenance therapy for AIDS-associated cryptococcal meningitis in 1999. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 31. Powderly WG, Saag MS, Cloud GA, Robinson P, Meyer RD, Jacobson JM, et al. conducted a controlled trial of fluconazole or amphotericin B to prevent relapse of cryptococcal meningitis in AIDS patients in 1992. Their study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 32. Beardsley J, Wolbers M, Kibengo FM, Ggayi A-BM, Kamali A, Cuc NTK, et al. evaluated the use of adjunctive dexamethasone in HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis in 2016. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 33. Bisson GP, Molefi M, Bellamy S, Thakur R, Steenhoff A, Tamuhla N, et al. studied the timing of ART initiation and cerebrospinal fluid fungal clearance in adults with HIV and cryptococcal meningitis in 2013. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 34. Boulware DR, Meya DB, Muzoor C, Rolfes MA, Huppler Hullsiek K, Musubire A, et al. investigated the timing of ART initiation after diagnosing cryptococcal meningitis in 2014. Their study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 35. Zolopa A, Andersen J, Powderly W, Sanchez A, Sanne I, Suckow C, et al. demonstrated that early ART reduces AIDS progression and death in individuals with acute opportunistic infections in 2009. Their findings were published in PLoS One. 36. Makadzange AT, Ndhlovu CE, Takarinda K, Reid M, Kurangwa M, Gona P, et al. compared early versus delayed ART initiation for concurrent HIV infection and cryptococcal meningitis in sub-Saharan Africa in 2010. Their study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 37. Bicanic T, Bottomley C, Loyse A, Brouwer AE, Muzoor C, Taseera K, et al. evaluated the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate-based induction therapy in HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis in 2015. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy. 38. Bahr NC, Rolfes MA, Musubire A, Nabeta H, Williams DA, Rhein J, et al. demonstrated that standardized electrolyte supplementation and fluid management improve survival during amphotericin therapy for cryptococcal meningitis in resource-limited settings in 2014. Their study was published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases. 39. Girmenia C, Cimino G, Di Cristofano F, Micozzi A, Gentile G, Martino P, et al. showed that hydration with salt repletion reduces renal toxicity of conventional amphotericin B therapy in patients with hematological malignancies in 2005. Their findings were published in Supportive Care in Cancer. 40. Thakur CP, Kumar A, Mitra DK, Roy A, Sinha AK, Ranjan A, et al. improved outcomes in kala-azar treatment by supplementing amphotericin B with physiologic saline and potassium chloride in 2010. Their study was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 41. Graybill JR, Sobel J, Saag M, Van Der Horst C, Powderly W, Cloud G, et al. provided guidelines for diagnosing and managing increased intracranial pressure in AIDS patients with cryptococcal meningitis in 2000. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 42. Rolfes MA, Hullsiek KH, Rhein J, Nabeta HW, Taseera K, Schutz C, et al. demonstrated the effect of therapeutic lumbar punctures on acute mortality from cryptococcal meningitis in 2014. Their study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 43. Haddow LJ, Colebunders R, Meintjes G, Lawn SD, Elliott JH, Manabe YC, et al. proposed clinical case definitions for cryptococcal immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome in HIV-1-infected individuals in 2010. Their findings were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 44. Kambugu A, Meya DB, Rhein J, O'Brien M, Janoff EN, Ronald AR, et al. evaluated outcomes of cryptococcal meningitis in Uganda before and after the availability of highly active ART in 2008. Their study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 45. Shelburne III SA, Darcourt J, White Jr AC, Greenberg SB, Hamill RJ, Atmar RL, et al. explored the role of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome in AIDS-related Cryptococcus neoformans disease in the era of highly active ART in 2005. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 46. Adenis A, Nacher M, Hanf M, Basurko C, Dufour J, Huber F, et al. compared tuberculosis and histoplasmosis among HIV-infected patients in 2014. Their study was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 47. Pasqualotto AC, Queiroz-Telles F highlighted histoplasmosis surpassing tuberculosis in Latin America in 2018. Their findings were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 48. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) and WHO provided guidelines for diagnosing and managing disseminated histoplasmosis among people living with HIV, accessed on June 1, 2021. 49. Caceres DH, Knuth M, Derado G, Lindsley MD conducted a meta-analysis in 2019 to evaluate assay performance for diagnosing progressive disseminated histoplasmosis in advanced HIV. Their findings were published in the Journal of Fungi (Basel). 50. Wheat LJ, Connolly-Stringfield PA, Baker RL, Curfman MF, Eads ME, Israel KS, et al. reviewed clinical findings, diagnosis, and treatment of disseminated histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in 1990. Their study was published in Medicine. 51. Johnson PC, Wheat LJ, Cloud GA, Goldman M, Lancaster D, Bamberger DM, et al. compared liposomal amphotericin B with conventional amphotericin B for induction therapy of histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in 2002. Their findings were published in the Annals of Internal Medicine. 52. Wheat LJ, Freifeld AG, Kleiman MB, Baddley JW, McKinsey DS, Loyd JE, et al. updated clinical practice guidelines for managing histoplasmosis in 2007. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 53. Murray M, Hine P reviewed treatment options for progressive disseminated histoplasmosis in people living with HIV in 2020. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 54. Wheat J, MaWhinney S, Hafner R, McKinsey D, Chen D, Korzun A, et al. evaluated fluconazole treatment for histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in 1997. Their study was published in the American Journal of Medicine. 55. Wheat J, Hafner R, Korzun AH, Limj MT, Spencer P, Larsen RA, et al. assessed itraconazole treatment for disseminated histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in 1995. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Medicine. 56. Norris S, Wheat J, McKinsey D, Lancaster D, Katz B, Black J, et al. demonstrated the prevention of histoplasmosis relapse with fluconazole in AIDS patients in 1994. Their study was published in the American Journal of Medicine. 57. Sharkey-Mathis PK, Velez J, Fetchick R, Graybill JR compared itraconazole and fluconazole for treating histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in 1993. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 58. Hecht FM, Wheat J, Korzun AH, Hafner R, Skahan KJ, Larsen R, et al. conducted a multicenter trial on itraconazole maintenance treatment for histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in 1997. Their study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 59. Myint T, Anderson AM, Sanchez A, Farabi A, Hage C, Baddley JW, et al. conducted a multicenter study in 2014 to evaluate outcomes and factors associated with histoplasmosis relapse in HIV/AIDS patients. Their findings were published in Medicine. 60. The WHO updated its policy on the lateral flow urine lipoarabinomannan assay (LF-LAM) for diagnosing active tuberculosis in people living with HIV, accessed on June 1, 2021. 61. User perspectives on LF-LAM testing were explored through qualitative research, as part of the WHO's policy update on LF-LAM for tuberculosis diagnosis in HIV patients. 62. The WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis screening and systematic screening for tuberculosis disease was accessed on June 1, 2021. 63. The WHO provided a package of care for children and adolescents with advanced HIV disease, as part of the STOP AIDS technical brief, accessed on June 1, 2021. 64. The WHO consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection were updated in their second edition, accessed on June 1, 2021. 65. The WHO issued recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience, accessed on June 1, 2021. 66. The WHO published guidelines on the public health response to pretreatment HIV drug resistance, accessed on June 1, 2021. 67. The WHO vaccine position papers were accessed for reference on June 1, 2021.
